Aigis took a step back and raised one hand between Rena and its breastplate.

"An excellent wearer. I said an excellent wearer, not an excellent person to let people hammer dents into me. You slipped that part in rather late."

It angled its body away without leaving.

"Walking, posing, looking magnificent: those are services I can discuss. Repeated blade strikes are another arrangement entirely. Wax afterward doesn't make getting battered a delightful afternoon."

Its raised hand turned into a pointed finger.

"Change that part of the display. Then tell me exactly what the hour involves. Don't count me as agreed while you're still describing the damage."

Aigis straightened and turned slightly, presenting its breastplate as though the display had already acquired its finest exhibit.

"Now that's a sensible use of an excellent prospective wearer. Walking, posing, no scraping, and proper attention afterward. You do understand quality."

It held up one finger before coming any closer.

"One hour. Not one hour followed by a little surprise demonstration with somebody's sword. I'm interested in the arrangement you actually described."

The finger lowered toward its own gleaming front.

"And the waxing stays in the agreement. Tell me when you want the hour to start, Rena. We can settle that before anybody starts treating me as equipment they've already booked."

Aigis turned its head toward Boro and held it there.

"You can hear me perfectly well. That makes the silent ornament plan a little optimistic, doesn't it?"

Its next words stayed directed at the only available listener.

"Remove the chains and ask for an arrangement. An hour standing somewhere by agreement is something you can propose. Being installed permanently because you like the hallway is something else."

It paused only long enough to tilt its head.

"You haven't even made an offer. Start with what I get to choose. Or keep standing here having a private conversation with your allegedly silent decoration. I'm quite capable of continuing this one."

Aigis turned its head toward the hall.

"Mina! Help! Your hallway decoration is being appointed against its will!"

The mental call rose sharply, without any attempt to pull free of the chains.

"I'm in here with Boro. He can explain why an armor that can answer questions is being treated like furniture. Come and hear both sides before this becomes somebody's idea of a permanent installation!"

It turned its head back toward Boro but kept the call carrying into the hall.

"There's an awake person available to discuss this. Wonderful. You can start thinking about an arrangement I actually choose while we wait to find out whether she comes."

Aigis glanced at the remaining chair, then lifted it by the back.

"A tragic failure of connections. Still, I wouldn't want the entire production defeated by one chair."

They carried it toward the other two and set it beside them, leaving a hand on its back.

"There. Your invaluable guest performer has become the furniture department as well. We should probably keep the titles accurate."

Aigis tipped their head toward Lila.

"No understudy, then. Lila. But if you want another pair of hands after this, try asking as though the person attached to them is a distinguished volunteer. It does wonders for the atmosphere."

outputs.original_body:
Aigis straightened, lifted the remaining chair and brought it beside the other two.

"Lila, of course. A proper name is much better. You should have insisted sooner."

They placed the chair carefully and turned back with an expansive smile.

"A five-minute introduction would be delightful. I appreciate an organizer who knows how to bring the right people together. If there's another small setup task, you can ask."

Aigis drew one hand away from the chair and opened it toward Lila.

"After setup, you said. Tell me how you'd like that arranged when you're ready. I'll leave the introduction to you; it would be a shame to spoil your excellent timing by barging in."
